words.sentence: To \(\underline{\text{abate}}\) her listlessness, she went for a long walk in the country.
words.solution: Abate means to reduce or lessen. Its opposite is increase. Lessen and subside are synonyms; sustain means to keep up, not to raise.

words.sentence: The oppressive pollution was noticed to have \(\underline{\text{abated}}\) after the unseasonal rainfall.
words.solution: 'Abated' means reduced in intensity; 'mitigated' is the nearest synonym meaning lessened. Common error: choosing 'suppressed' which implies forceful stopping. Matches option A: mitigated.

To abound is to exist in large numbers, to be plentiful or to thrive in plenty. Flourish (grow abundantly, thrive) is the closest. Increase means to become greater, not to be plentiful; succeed is unrelated, and adequate is an adjective meaning just enough.

words.sentence: They live in the apartment \(\underline{\text{above}}\) ours.
words.solution: Above means at a higher level; its opposite is below. Over and upward are near-synonyms, and after is about time or order.
"Absurd" means wildly unreasonable or ridiculous. Its opposite is "sensible" (reasonable). Tolerable, adorable and lovable are not opposites of absurd.

words.sentence: I do not have any \(\underline{\text{access}}\) to the information in this matter.
words.solution: Access is the right or means of reaching something. Its opposite is denial (being refused it). Reach is a near-synonym; clue and doubt are unrelated.

words.sentence: He is always \(\underline{\text{active}}\) in a party but _______ in the class.
words.solution: Inert means inactive or without movement, the opposite of active: active in a party but inert in the class.

words.sentence: Businessmen who lack \(\underline{\text{acumen}}\) cannot be expected to be very successful.
words.solution: 'Acumen' means the ability to make good judgements; 'sharpness' (keenness/shrewdness) is the closest synonym. 'Fairness' and 'righteousness' relate to ethics, not mental agility. Matches option B: sharpness.

words.sentence: Do you know the old \(\underline{\text{adage}}\) 'the show must go on’?
words.solution:
**Note:** None of the options is a true antonym of "adage". The answer shown follows SSC's answer key.

An adage is a traditional saying that expresses an accepted truth. No option is a true opposite. Misconstruction, a mistaken interpretation, stands against a saying accepted as true, which makes it the closest contrast; rebuke (scolding), dare (challenge) and addiction have no link to the word.

words.sentence: It takes time to \(\underline{\text{adapt}}\) to a new environment.
words.solution: To adapt to something is to adjust to new conditions. Apply, understand and control do not carry that meaning.

words.sentence: They will not \(\underline{\text{admit}}\) children under fourteen.
words.solution: Answer: B. Here 'admit' means to let someone in, not to confess something. That rules out 'avow' and 'concede', which are about admitting a fact. Both 'receive' and 'accept' can mean letting a person in (a school accepts or receives pupils), so two options are defensible. 'Receive' is the keyed answer because it stays closest to the idea of letting someone enter a place.

words.sentence: The leader said, "I am \(\underline{\text{aghast}}\) with the developments so far. I will take time to understand this."
words.solution: Answer: D. 'Aghast' means shocked or horrified; 'horrified' is the nearest synonym.
"Alert" means watchful and quick to notice danger, which is "vigilant". "Dull" and "inactive" are nearly opposite, and "smart" means clever or well dressed.

words.sentence: Elisabeth stood at the piano, which did nothing to **allay** his anxiety.
words.solution: To allay is to calm or lessen a fear or worry. Aggravate (make worse) is the opposite; mitigate and mollify are synonyms, and simplify is unrelated.
Apathy is a lack of interest, feeling or concern, that is, indifference. Empathy is sharing another's feelings, while aversion and hostility are active dislike, not the absence of feeling.
Apogee means the highest point or climax (originally the point of an orbit farthest from the Earth). Peak is its synonym. Nadir and base are opposites, and start does not fit.

words.sentence: Ramya is an \(\underline{\text{ardent}}\) follower of secularism.
words.solution: "Ardent" means passionate and devoted, so an ardent follower is a committed one. "Forced", "temporary" and "unhappy" have nothing to do with keen devotion.

words.sentence: For Gandhiji, India's religious and linguistic diversity was an \(\underline{\text{asset}}\), not a liability.
words.solution: Answer: B. 'Asset' (a valuable thing, contrasted with liability) is nearest to 'advantage'. Attribute is a quality (close but not the contrast intended); advantage best fits the 'asset vs liability' opposition.
Astute means shrewd and clever. Its opposite is stupid. The other words are unrelated.
To attack is to act against someone aggressively; the opposite is defence (protecting against attack). An ambush is a surprise attack and an engagement is a battle, so both are close in sense.

words.sentence: Most of the land near the town is \(\underline{\text{barren}}\), but the efforts of the farmers have turned it ________.
words.solution: Barren land cannot produce crops; the opposite is fertile. Sterile, unfruitful and infertile are synonyms of barren.

words.sentence: \(\underline{\text{Beauty}}\) lies in the eyes of the beholder.
words.solution: Answer: C. Antonym of 'Beauty' (loveliness, charm) is 'Inelegance' (lack of grace/beauty). 'Allure' and 'Charm' are synonyms; 'Ideal' is unrelated.

words.sentence: He is \(\underline{\text{biased}}\) against the students from cities.
words.solution: 'Biased' means unfairly prejudiced; its antonym is 'impartial' (treating all equally). Matches option D: impartial.

words.sentence: In the winters, the countryside view is \(\underline{\text{bleak}}\) and the house is drafty.
words.solution: 'Bleak' means lacking vegetation, or cold and miserable. Its antonym is 'verdant' (green with vegetation, lush). Matches option B: verdant.

words.sentence: \(\underline{\text{Blend}}\) the grains to make a smooth paste.
words.solution: Answer: A. 'Blend' = mix/combine. The opposite is 'separate'. 'Mingle', 'coalesce', 'amalgamate' are synonyms of blend.

words.sentence: Most of the flowers \(\underline{\text{bloom}}\) in the spring season but they start to ________ during summer.
words.solution: To bloom is to flower and flourish; the opposite is to wither (dry up and fade). Flourish and blossom are synonyms of bloom, and flush (to redden or to rinse) is unrelated.

words.sentence: There was much to \(\underline{\text{boast}}\) about the quality of his work.
words.solution: Answer: C. Boast = praise/extol oneself; opposite = deprecate (express disapproval/belittle). Bluster/brag/flaunt are synonyms.

words.sentence: His \(\underline{\text{bounty}}\) is limitless.
words.solution: 'Bounty' means generosity or liberality in giving; 'benevolence' (goodwill and generosity) is the nearest synonym. Matches option A: benevolence.

words.sentence: None but the \(\underline{\text{brave}}\) deserves the fair.
words.solution: 'Brave' means courageous; its antonym is 'coward' (someone lacking courage). Matches option B: coward.

words.sentence: The Managing Director of the company declared that he is \(\underline{\text{broke}}\) and there is a need to seek support from the government.
words.solution: The key concept is synonym identification. 'Broke' in informal usage means having no money; 'bankrupt' is the closest formal synonym. Matches option A: bankrupt.
A bully is a person who intimidates or harms weaker people, that is, an oppressor. Coddle (to pamper) is nearly the opposite; oxen and plough are distractors from "bull".

words.sentence: He was riding his bike on a \(\underline{\text{bumpy}}\) surface.
words.solution: Bumpy means uneven and jolting. Jerky, uneven and choppy are near-synonyms; steady (firm, smooth, not shaking) is the only opposite offered.

words.sentence: Mr. Kumar works as a \(\underline{\text{bursar}}\) in the sports academy.
words.solution: A bursar is a person who manages the financial affairs of an institution; the closest synonym is 'accountant'. Matches option B: accountant.
Callow describes a young person who is inexperienced and immature (a callow youth). Experienced, wise and mature are close to its opposite.
"Candid" means frank and open in speech. Its opposite is "guarded", cautious and careful not to reveal much. "Frank", "honest" and "open" are synonyms of candid.
To cavil is to raise petty, trivial objections, which is to quibble. Praise and approve are close to its opposite; ignore is unrelated.

words.sentence: Women gather in the community park on a regular basis to \(\underline{\text{chant}}\) prayers for the benefit of all.
words.solution: 'Chant' means to say or sing repeatedly; 'recite' is the nearest synonym in the context of prayers. Matches option D: recite.

words.sentence: The house was full of \(\underline{\text{chaos}}\) when I reached.
words.solution: Answer: D. Chaos is opposite to order. Disorder/confusion are synonyms; uniformity is sameness, not the direct opposite of disorder.

words.sentence: She \(\underline{\text{chided}}\) her son for being impatient with the customers.
words.solution: To chide is to scold or rebuke. Reproved, scolded and rebuked are synonyms; applauded (praised) is the opposite.
Clear (transparent, letting light through) is opposite to opaque (not letting light through). Clean, mess and untidy relate to tidiness, not to clarity.

words.sentence: Mr. Sen is \(\underline{\text{clever}}\) enough to handle his professional hazards.
words.solution: The denotation (literal dictionary meaning) of "clever" is quick to understand and learn, that is "intelligent": "Mr. Sen is intelligent enough to handle his professional hazards." "Bold" means brave, "callous" means unfeeling and "foolish" is the opposite.
Cogent means clear, logical and convincing (a cogent argument). Weak, dubious and unclear are close to its opposite.
"Covert" means secret or concealed. Its opposite is "overt", done openly. "Secret", "hidden" and "clandestine" are synonyms.

words.sentence: He is essentially a \(\underline{\text{crude}}\) person.
words.solution: 'Crude' means rough or unrefined. Its antonym is 'refined'. Matches option B: refined.

words.sentence: He was very \(\underline{\text{cruel}}\) in dealing with the students.
words.solution: Cruel means causing pain without pity; its opposite is kind. Malevolent (wishing harm) is close to cruel, skittish means nervous or easily scared, and kingly means royal.

"Dainty" means delicately small, pretty and graceful, so the closest synonym is "elegant". "Vulgar" is the opposite, "sable" means black (or a small animal), and "fine" overlaps only in its sense of delicate.

words.sentence: The \(\underline{\text{dearth}}\) of governmental policies on the basic rights and comforts of the impaired population leads to low standard of public life in a country.
words.solution: Dearth means a scarcity or lack. Its opposite is abundance (plenty). Paucity and lacunae (gaps) are close to dearth in meaning, and brevity means shortness.

words.sentence: The biggest \(\underline{\text{debate}}\) among scientists today is about \(\textit{\text{cloud feedback}}\).
words.solution: The antonym of 'debate' (a formal discussion with opposing viewpoints) is 'agreement' (consensus, accord). Matches option D: agreement.

words.sentence: Early medieval period was not a combination of urban and rural civilization. It was not a period of urban \(\underline{\text{decay}}\) as claimed by some.
words.solution: Answer: A. 'Decay' means decline or deterioration; its opposite is 'survival' (growth/flourishing). The other options are near-synonyms of decay.

words.sentence: The \(\underline{\text{deluge}}\) affected the population.
words.solution: 'Deluge' means a heavy flood or downpour; its antonym is 'drought' (absence of rain). Matches option B: drought.
To demur is to raise an objection or show reluctance. Oppose, object and resist are near-synonyms; agree is the opposite.

words.sentence: She is considered to be \(\underline{\text{demure}}\) by her family members.
words.solution: Answer: C. 'Demure' means modest/reserved; its opposite is 'brazen' (bold/shameless).

words.sentence: Hitler was a \(\underline{\text{despot}}\).
words.solution: The key concept is synonym identification. 'Despot' means a ruler with absolute power; 'dictator' is the closest synonym. Matches option B: dictator.

words.sentence: The hotel room had \(\underline{\text{dingy}}\) walls.
words.solution: Answer: B. 'Dingy' means gloomy, dull, and dirty. The nearest in meaning is 'dark and dirty'.

words.sentence: The musician gave a \(\underline{\text{dismal}}\) performance of a few old melodies at last night’s concert.
words.solution: Dismal means gloomy, dull or depressing. Lively (full of energy and spirit) is its opposite. Melancholy is close to a synonym.
To dodge is to avoid something, by a quick movement or by cunning (dodge a question). The other options are unrelated.

words.sentence: The \(\underline{\text{dodgy}}\) behaviour of the leader led to her fall
words.solution: Dodgy = suspicious; nearest synonym among options is dubious. Matches option B.

words.sentence: The confectioner \(\underline{\text{dusted}}\) a fine layer of sugar on the muffin.
words.solution: Here dusted means sprinkled a fine powder over something. Scattered, sprinkled and powdered all say much the same. Cleaned (removing a layer from a surface) is the opposite of covering it with a layer, so it is the answer.
To "efface" is to erase or wipe out a mark or memory, so "destroy" is the nearest meaning. "Hidden" only means out of sight, and "makeup" and "daily" are unrelated.

words.sentence: She was \(\underline{\text{elated}}\) about her promotion, but her colleague felt quite disheartened.
words.solution: Elated means very happy and excited. Delighted and cheerful are synonyms; discouraged (dispirited, as the sentence's "disheartened" also signals) is the opposite.
The opposite of an enemy is a friend. Attacker and combatant are close to enemy, and a colleague is simply a co-worker.

To "entail" is to involve something as a necessary part or result, that is, to "necessitate" it: "The job entails long hours." "Assume" means suppose, "eliminate" means remove, and "flaw" is a defect.
Entire means whole or complete, so its opposite is incomplete. Undivided and thorough are close in meaning; ingress means entry.
A eulogy is a speech or piece of writing that praises someone, often someone who has died: a tribute. Criticism, insult and condemnation are close to its opposite.
To evoke is to bring a feeling or memory to mind, to call forth or produce it; induce (bring about) is closest. Abandon, reduce and divert do not mean this.
To extol is to praise highly. Reward means to give something in return for merit, which is not the same as praising, and punish and dismay are unrelated.

words.sentence: Ram \(\underline{\text{failed}}\) initially but after a few years, he _________ in every field.
words.solution: The opposite of failed is succeeded, and "succeeded in every field" completes the contrast set up by "but".
Fatal means causing death, that is, deadly. Additional, easy and jovial (cheerful) are unrelated.
Feeble means lacking strength, that is weak. Strong is its antonym, unheedful means careless, and baneful means harmful.

words.sentence: My first lecture in the classroom was a \(\underline{\text{fiasco}}\).
words.solution: 'Fiasco' means a complete failure; its antonym is 'success'. 'Disaster' is a synonym, 'joy' and 'fun' are unrelated. Matches option A: success.

words.sentence: The \(\underline{\text{fickle}}\) nature of humans is at times the cause of great innovations.
words.solution: 'Fickle' means changing frequently; the nearest synonym is 'vacillating' (indecisive, changing). Matches option A: vacillating.
Fierce means violent, intense or aggressive. Gentle is the opposite; fanatic and fraud are unrelated.
"Filthy" means very dirty. "Tidy" and "shiny" suggest the opposite, and "visual" means relating to sight.

words.sentence: The government's new policies will come into force from the next \(\underline{\text{fiscal}}\) year.
words.solution: Fiscal relates to government finances or revenue; financial is the closest synonym. Matches option C: financial.

words.sentence: One should \(\underline{\text{follow}}\) the role models in life.
words.solution: To follow a role model is to copy or imitate them, which is to emulate. Admire and cherish are feelings, not actions of following, and reward does not fit.

To foment is to stir up or instigate (trouble, unrest). Its opposite is to keep in check or control, which "regulate" gives. Separation, remoteness and proximity are about distance and have no link to the word.
Forbid means to refuse to permit; its opposite is allow. Prohibit is a synonym, and call and forsake (abandon) are unrelated.

words.sentence: His \(\underline{\text{frail}}\) appearance was considered a merit.
words.solution: 'Frail' means weak or delicate; its antonym is 'sturdy' (strong and robust). Options A and B are synonyms of frail. Matches option C: sturdy.
"Frugal" means careful and sparing with money, so "thrifty". "Lavish", "extravagant" and "wasteful" all mean spending freely, the opposite.

words.sentence: The movie is about \(\underline{\text{fusion}}\) of old and contemporary ideas.
words.solution: Answer: C. 'Fusion' = merging/blending together. The opposite is 'separation'. 'Joining', 'bonding', 'blending' are synonyms.
"Futile" means producing no result, useless. Its opposite is "effective" (producing the intended result). "Useless", "pointless" and "vain" are synonyms of futile.

words.sentence: If you listen carefully you'll discover that the soundtrack is \(\underline{\text{fuzzy}}\) in places.
words.solution: Answer: C. Of a sound, fuzzy means indistinct or blurred, so clear is its opposite. Distorted and vague restate it.
Genial means friendly and cheerful in manner. Despondent is the opposite; optimistic and positive describe hopeful outlook, not a pleasant, cheerful manner.
Gentle means kind, mild and tender. Of the options only sympathetic (kind, caring) is close; fierce, ferocious and cruel are its opposites.
Glory is great honour and fame. Its opposite is *shame* (disgrace). Honour is a near-synonym, delight means great pleasure, and gluttony means overeating.

"Grisly" means causing horror or disgust, gruesome: "a grisly murder". "Atrocious" (horrifyingly wicked or shocking) is the closest match. "Dire" means extremely serious or urgent ("dire need"), not horrifying; "pleasant" and "glorious" are opposite in tone.

words.sentence: His mother never held a **grudge** against his father.
words.solution: The sheet prints the whole sentence in bold, so no single word stands out; the word the options answer is "grudge" (lasting ill will or resentment). Its opposite is benevolence (goodwill, kindness). Malevolence and rancour mean much the same as grudge, and revulsion is disgust.
Grumpy means bad-tempered and easily annoyed, which is irritable. Friendly, polite and calm are near-opposites.

words.sentence: He worked alone as he did not want anyone to \(\underline{\text{hamper}}\) his project.
words.solution: "Hamper" means to hinder or obstruct; its opposite is **help**. "Impede" is a synonym of hamper, and "care" and "finish" are not opposites.

words.sentence: I was \(\underline{\text{happy}}\) to know that Sheila passed her final exams.
words.solution: The opposite of happy is sad. Upbeat and joyful are synonyms, and excited is close in feeling.

words.sentence: We’d better watch our step and not give him any excuse to **harass** us further.
words.solution: The sheet prints the whole sentence in bold, so no single word stands out; the only word the options can match is "harass" (to pressure or torment repeatedly). Intimidate (frighten, threaten) is the closest. Soothe is nearly opposite; betray and relish are unrelated.

words.sentence: The truck was carrying a \(\underline{\text{heavy}}\) load .
words.solution: The opposite of a heavy load is a light load. Big, massive and large are close in meaning to heavy.
To hinder is to obstruct or make difficult; to facilitate is to make easier. Block is a synonym; praise and joy are unrelated.

words.sentence: He was the most \(\underline{\text{honest}}\) and good-hearted man that she had ever met.
words.solution: Honest means truthful and genuine, which is sincere. Deceptive and fake are opposites; biased is unrelated.

To be "immune" is to be resistant to (unaffected by) a disease or influence: "immune to criticism" means resistant to it. "Safe" is close but only describes being out of danger, not the resisting itself; "asleep" and "variable" are unrelated.

words.sentence: Learning of foreign language should not \(\underline{\text{impede}}\) one's mother tongue learning.
words.solution: Answer: C. Impede means to obstruct or hinder. 'Hinder' is the direct synonym; 'facilitate' is the opposite.

words.sentence: According to G B Shaw, men have become \(\underline{\text{inert}}\). Therefore, life force has chosen women to perform its functions.
words.solution: Answer: A. Antonym of 'inert' (inactive, motionless) is 'lively' (active, energetic). Quiescent, dormant and apathetic are synonyms of inert.
Innate means inborn, present from birth. Its opposite is learned (acquired through experience). Natural is a synonym; aquatic and replete are unrelated.
To insert is to put something in; to remove is to take it out. Inject is close to a synonym.

words.sentence: The Professor has been able to \(\underline{\text{instil}}\) confidence in her students
words.solution: Instil = to gradually introduce/infuse; nearest synonym is inculcate (to teach by repetition). Matches option A.

Jargon is special words used by a particular group that outsiders find hard to understand. Slang (informal words of a particular group) is the closest. Verboseness is wordiness, formality and eloquence are unrelated.

words.sentence: We are planning a \(\underline{\text{jaunt}}\) for a while during the winter.
words.solution: Answer: C. A jaunt is a short trip or excursion — nearest to expedition.

words.sentence: The teammates made several \(\underline{\text{jibes}}\) at the opponent team members during the interview.
words.solution:
**Note:** None of the options is a true antonym of "jibes". The answer shown follows SSC's answer key.

A jibe is an insulting or mocking remark. Mockery (D) is a synonym. None of the other options is a clean opposite such as 'praise' or 'compliment'. SSC's key gives B (Contradict); consolation (C), words of comfort, is the nearest opposite in meaning.
Jovial means cheerful and friendly. Miserable and solemnity are near opposites, and profane means disrespectful of sacred things.

words.sentence: Instead of becoming \(\underline{\text{joyous}}\) to hear the breaking news, she became _________ .
words.solution: "Instead of" sets up a contrast with joyous, so the blank needs its opposite: melancholic (sad). Ecstatic and exuberant are synonyms of joyous; vengeful is unrelated.
Kilter means good working order or balance, as in "out of kilter". Anarchy, shambles and disrepair are all states of disorder.
Labour is hard work, and toil means hard, continuous work. Relaxation and dalliance (idle time-wasting) are close to the opposite; mesh is a net-like material.
To lament is to mourn or express grief; the opposite is to celebrate. Deplore, decry and regret all express disapproval or sorrow, so they lie on the same side as lament.

words.sentence: An elephant is a \(\underline{\text{large}}\) mammal.
words.solution: The opposite of large is tiny. Bumper and gigantic mean large, and heroic is unrelated.

words.sentence: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. Gentlemen always go for a \(\underline{\text{lawful}}\) approach, but rouges choose ______ ways to solve problems.
words.solution: "Lawful" means permitted by law; its opposite is "illicit" (forbidden by law). "Legitimate" and "legal" are synonyms of "lawful", and "sophisticated" is unrelated.

words.sentence: Those streets are very \(\underline{\text{lonely}}\).
words.solution: Lonely streets are deserted, with few people. The opposite is crowded. Isolated, empty and remote are close in meaning to lonely.
Loving means showing love or warmth, the same as affectionate. Offish (distant, aloof) is nearly the opposite; rejuvenate and subordinate are unrelated.

words.sentence: Lucy presented a \(\underline{\text{lucid}}\) account of her achievements before the committee.
words.solution: Lucid means clear and easy to understand. Ambiguous (open to more than one meaning, unclear) is the opposite. Orderly, intelligible and transparent are close to its meaning.

words.sentence: It is sheer \(\underline{\text{lunacy}}\) to drive a car in this frosty weather.
words.solution: 'Lunacy' means extreme foolishness or mental illness. 'Insanity' is its direct synonym. Matches option C: insanity.

words.sentence: This is his \(\underline{\text{maiden}}\) appearance on the screen.
words.solution: 'Maiden' means first or earliest. His maiden appearance means his first appearance. Matches option A: first.

words.sentence: Ravi told his friend that he had no intention to \(\underline{\text{malign}}\) him.
words.solution: 'Malign' means to speak about someone in a spitefully critical manner (i.e., to slander). The closest synonym is 'slander'. Matches option B: slander.

words.sentence: She deftly \(\underline{\text{masked}}\) her feelings.
words.solution: Answer: A. To mask one's feelings is to conceal/hide them. "Hid" is the direct synonym. "Obscured" can mean to make unclear but "hid" is the nearest in meaning to mask (to cover/conceal). "Flaunted" is opposite.

Memory is the faculty of remembering; oblivion is the state of forgetting or being forgotten, its opposite. Retrospection (looking back on the past) is close to memory, and suppress and impart are verbs unrelated in meaning.
Merit is the quality of being good or worthy of praise, which is a virtue. Fatigue is tiredness, residue is what is left over, and oblique means slanting or indirect.

words.sentence: Her room looks very \(\underline{\text{messy}}\)
words.solution: Messy means untidy or disordered; its opposite is organised (neat, in order). Untidy, chaotic and disordered are synonyms of messy.
"Mighty" means very strong and powerful; its opposite is "weak". "Forcible" and "forceful" are close to its meaning, and "haughty" means arrogant.

words.sentence: The experts' \(\underline{\text{minute}}\) examination brought to light some important clues.
words.solution: 'Minute' (adjective) means extremely small or precise; here it means very detailed. Matches option B: detailed.

words.sentence: His **modest** nature made all the difference.
words.solution: A modest person is unassuming and does not boast; of the options, shy (reserved, retiring) comes closest. Courageous, horrific and dry are unrelated.
Morbid means having an unhealthy interest in gloomy or unpleasant subjects such as death, so gloomy is the closest. Blithe (cheerful, carefree) is nearly the opposite; grand and bet are unrelated.

words.sentence: She sat there looking \(\underline{\text{morose}}\).
words.solution: Answer: A. Morose means gloomy and sullen, so cheerful is its opposite. Melancholic and sullen are synonyms of it.

words.sentence: A strong man is a mediator between divine and **mortal** fate.
words.solution: Mortal can mean deadly or causing death (a mortal wound), and lethal means the same. Delightful, sincere and overjoyed have no link to the word.
To mourn is to feel or show deep sorrow, especially for someone who has died; "grieve" means the same. "Dread" is to fear, "amuse" is to entertain, and "approve" is to agree with.

words.sentence: He could not \(\underline{\text{muster}}\) courage to speak the truth before his friend.
words.solution: The key concept is synonym identification. 'Muster' means to gather or summon; 'gather' is the closest synonym. Matches option C: gather.

words.sentence: The coach was of the opinion that his erstwhile protégé was approaching the \(\underline{\text{nadir}}\) of his career.
words.solution: Answer: A. Nadir means the lowest point — the all-time low. Zenith and prime are opposites.

words.sentence: It was a mystery as to where the young girl had acquired such a \(\underline{\text{naive}}\) belief.
words.solution: Answer: C. "Naive" means innocent/unsophisticated/lacking experience or judgement; its opposite is "wise" (experienced, having good judgement). "Credulous", "childlike" and "innocent" are near-synonyms, not antonyms.

words.sentence: He loves doing \(\underline{\text{nasty}}\) things.
words.solution: The key concept is synonym identification. 'Nasty' means unpleasant or offensive; 'foul' is the closest synonym. Matches option C: foul.

words.sentence: He had the \(\underline{\text{nerve}}\) to face the robbers all alone.
words.solution:
'Nerve' here means boldness to face danger.
Option (D) courage has the same sense.
Option (A) strength, (B) capacity and (C) stupidity do not give this meaning.
So the answer is (D) courage.

words.sentence: Ranen feels that the \(\underline{\text{notion}}\) of democracy is a farce.
words.solution: A notion is an idea or belief held in the mind. Its opposite is reality, what actually exists. Quotient, law and portion are unrelated in meaning.

words.sentence: The Arabs who are not in the cities live in the desert throughout the year, shifting from one \(\underline{\text{oasis}}\) to another.
words.solution: An 'oasis' is a fertile spot in a desert where water is available, often from a spring; 'spring' is the closest in meaning as the source of water. Matches option D: spring.

words.sentence: I \(\underline{\text{object}}\) the false claims made against me.
words.solution: To object is to express disapproval or opposition. To assent is to express agreement, the opposite. Ease, restore and ascertain (find out for certain) are unrelated.

words.sentence: He was too \(\underline{\text{obtuse}}\) to understand the merits of the case.
words.solution: Answer: D. 'Obtuse' (of a person) means slow to understand, dull-witted. The nearest synonym is 'dull'. 'Quick witted' is the antonym.
To oppugn is to call something into question, to dispute or attack it. Question, dispute and challenge are synonyms; defend (support, uphold) is the opposite.
To "pacify" is to calm someone down or make them less angry, which is to "soothe" them. "Rebuke" and "blame" mean to criticise, and "strengthen" means to make stronger.

words.sentence: For Rana, unable to see a thing, the \(\underline{\text{parade}}\) seemed to last forever.
words.solution: A "parade" is a public procession of people moving in line, so its synonym is "procession". The other options pick up the idea of not seeing ("darkness", "concealment", "hiding") but do not mean parade.

words.sentence: She is a \(\underline{\text{patron}}\) of art and culture.
words.solution: Patron means a person who supports or sponsors someone; 'backer' is the closest synonym. Matches option D: backer.

words.sentence: His last days were spent in great \(\underline{\text{penury}}\).
words.solution:
'Penury' means extreme poverty. 'Poverty' has the same meaning.
'Affluence' means wealth, the opposite. 'Pain' and 'activity' do not mean poverty.
So the answer is (A) poverty.

words.sentence: \(\underline{\text{Permit}}\) me to present you with a book.
words.solution: 'Permit' means to allow; its antonym is 'prohibit' (to forbid). Matches option C: prohibit.
To peruse is to read or examine something carefully, so check is the closest. Pursue is a look-alike trap meaning to follow or chase; draw and narrate are unrelated.

words.sentence: The \(\underline{\text{placid}}\) conversation between the two cricketers on a TV show aroused much controversy.
words.solution: "Placid" means calm and not easily excited, so its opposite is "angry". "Sardonic" means mocking, "inappropriate" means unsuitable and "informal" means casual; none is the opposite of calm.

words.sentence: Spring is a time of \(\underline{\text{plenty}}\).
words.solution: Plenty means abundance; its antonym is 'scarcity' meaning a shortage. Matches option B: scarcity.

words.sentence: I understand your \(\underline{\text{plight}}\).
words.solution: A plight is a difficult or unfortunate situation. Predicament, dilemma and quandary are synonyms; an advantage, a favourable position, is the opposite.

words.sentence: If you \(\underline{\text{ponder}}\) the matter you are likely to arrive at the appropriate conclusion.
words.solution: Answer: B. To ponder is to think carefully about something, so to ignore it is the opposite. Mull is a synonym, defer concerns timing and rethink still involves thought.
To purify is to make clean; to pollute is to make impure. Wash is close to a synonym; chant and invite are unrelated.

"Quaint" means attractively unusual or old-fashioned; its opposite is "ordinary" (common, unremarkable). "Brisk" means quick, "ridiculous" means absurd, and "distinct" means clearly different, which is nearer to "quaint" than opposite.
To quell is to put down or calm (quell a riot, quell fears). Suppress, subdue and restrain are synonyms; provoke (stir up, incite) is the opposite.
"Rapid" means fast; its opposite is "slow". "Active" and "smart" are not opposites of speed, and "lately" means recently.

words.sentence: She \(\underline{\text{rarely}}\) comes here.
words.solution: Rarely means not often; its antonym is 'always' meaning at all times. A common mistake is choosing 'frequently' but 'always' is the stronger opposite. Matches option C: always.

To reckon is first of all to count or calculate ("reckon the cost"); it also means to think or consider. Count is its direct synonym. Assess means to judge the worth of something, which is close but not the core meaning, and merit is unrelated.

words.sentence: Is there any portal to \(\underline{\text{redeem}}\) these coupons that I have collected from the store?
words.solution: To redeem a coupon is to exchange it and claim what it is worth. To forfeit is to lose the right to something, the opposite of claiming it. Forsake (abandon), deplore (condemn) and embezzle (steal funds in one's care) do not oppose it.

words.sentence: I \(\underline{\text{refuse}}\) to let anything come in the way of my dreams.
words.solution: To refuse is to decline to allow something. Its opposite here is permit (allow): "I permit anything to come in the way" reverses the sense. Balk (hesitate, refuse) is a near-synonym, repress means to hold back, and accord means to agree or grant, which does not fit "to let ...".

words.sentence: The decision of the Union Government to \(\underline{\text{repeal}}\) the Urban Land Ceiling Act has been welcomed by all.
words.solution: 'Repeal' means to revoke or cancel a law officially. Matches option C: cancel.

words.sentence: This is such a \(\underline{\text{rowdy}}\) classroom.
words.solution: Rowdy means noisy and disorderly. Compliant (obedient, well-behaved) is the opposite; the other three are near-synonyms.

words.sentence: She had a \(\underline{\text{ruddy}}\), open face and an oddly guileless manner.
words.solution: 'Ruddy' means having a healthy red complexion; its antonym is 'cadaverous' (pale, like a corpse). Matches option B: cadaverous.
Scary means causing fear; comforting means easing fear or worry, the opposite. Awful is close in meaning, and bright and pristine are unrelated.

words.sentence: Identity the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Secure
words.solution: To secure something is to make it safe or protect it. Attack (to assail or try to harm) is the opposite. Save is close in meaning, while trundle (roll slowly) and succeed are unrelated.

words.sentence: \(\underline{\text{Seldom}}\) had he been so joyous in other’s happiness.
words.solution: Seldom means rarely. Its opposite is frequently (often). Hardly and rarely are near-synonyms, and occasionally is close in meaning too.

words.sentence: The \(\underline{\text{serene}}\) beauty of Kashmir had a soothing effect on his mind.
words.solution: The word 'serene' means calm and peaceful; its antonym is 'turbulent' — characterized by conflict or confusion. Matches option D: turbulent.

words.sentence: They \(\underline{\text{served}}\) fruits after the dinner.
words.solution: Answer: D. To serve food/fruits is to present or offer it to others; "offered" is the nearest synonym in this context. "Waited" (as in wait on) is less direct than offered.

words.sentence: It is unwise to \(\underline{\text{sever}}\) diplomatic relations with a neighbouring country over small matters.
words.solution: 'Sever' means to cut or break off; 'cut off' is the closest synonym. 'Estrange' means to cause to feel alienated (related but not equivalent), 'engage' is an antonym. Matches option C: cut off.

words.sentence: Mr. Satterthwaite was \(\underline{\text{shrewd}}\) enough to penetrate her meaning.
words.solution: "Shrewd" means sharp in judgement and quick to understand, that is, smart. "Innocent" is nearly its opposite, and "aged" and "funny" are unrelated.

words.sentence: The newly made road was \(\underline{\text{smooth}}\).
words.solution: 'Smooth' means even and flat; its antonym is 'rutted' (having ruts, uneven). Options B and C do not directly mean rough/uneven as a surface. Matches option A: rutted.

words.sentence: The baby could not move as the place was \(\underline{\text{soggy}}\).
words.solution: Answer: B. 'Soggy' means saturated/wet. Its antonym is 'Dry'. (Sodden and Wet are synonyms.)

words.sentence: At last she was able to get some \(\underline{\text{solace}}\) as the matter has been resolved amicably.
words.solution: Answer: D. 'Solace' means comfort or consolation in distress. Its opposite is 'aggravation' (worsening of distress). 'comfort' and 'relief' are synonyms; 'punishment' is unrelated.

words.sentence: After the mishap, the mood was \(\underline{\text{sombre}}\) among the survivors.
words.solution: Sombre has two senses - dark in colour, and gloomy or grave in mood. Here it describes a mood, so the opposite required is buoyant: cheerful and light-hearted. Shady and dingy belong to the colour sense and are in fact close to sombre rather than opposed to it, and restrained is nearer to sombre than against it.

words.sentence: Too many cooks \(\underline{\text{spoil}}\) the broth.
words.solution: 'Spoil' means to damage or ruin; its antonym is 'embellish' (to enhance or beautify). Matches option C: embellish.

words.sentence: Aunt May thought that Uncle Ken’s job as a manager at Firpo’s hotel in Shimla was a \(\underline{\text{stable}}\) one.
words.solution: "Stable" means firm and unlikely to change, so its opposite is "mutable" (liable to change). "Permanent" and "durable" are near synonyms, and "lucrative" means profitable.

words.sentence: The new Principal of the school is \(\underline{\text{stern}}\), yet he understands the needs of his subordinates.
words.solution: "Stern" means strict and severe; its opposite is "lenient", meaning tolerant and not strict. "Flippant" means not serious, "desolate" means bleak and "noxious" means harmful.

words.sentence: The jewels have been \(\underline{\text{stolen}}\) from her bedroom.
words.solution: Answer: A. "Stolen" = taken dishonestly; "embezzled" (to steal/misappropriate, especially money or valuables in one's trust) is the nearest in meaning. The other options are unrelated.

words.sentence: I will \(\underline{\text{strive}}\) to win the race.
words.solution: To "strive" is to make a great effort, that is, to try hard: "attempt". "Trouble", "support" and "assume" do not mean to try.

words.sentence: One must be very \(\underline{\text{strong}}\) to lift this box of glass jars.
words.solution: The opposite of strong is weak. Mighty and rugged are close in meaning to strong; complicated is unrelated.

words.sentence: The apple tasted incredibly \(\underline{\text{sweet}}\) .
words.solution: Of the tastes, the opposite of sweet is bitter. Delicious and pleasant are close in sense to sweet here, and special is unrelated.

words.sentence: In front of the big screen, this behaviour is generally considered \(\underline{\text{taboo}}\).
words.solution: Taboo describes something forbidden or socially unacceptable. Its opposite is acceptable, which also fits the sentence ("considered acceptable").
"Tacit" means understood or implied without being stated. Its opposite is "explicit", stated clearly and openly. "Implicit", "unstated" and "understood" are near-synonyms of "tacit".

"Tight" means firmly stretched or fixed; its opposite is "slack", loose and not stretched. "Cordial" means warm and friendly, "comfortable" means at ease, and "resilient" means able to recover quickly.

"Timid" means lacking courage, easily frightened; its direct opposite is "audacious" (daring, fearlessly bold). "Assertive" (confident in stating one's views) and "resolute" (firm in purpose) are less exact opposites, and "blunt" means outspoken or not sharp.
Toxic means poisonous, harmful enough to kill, so lethal is the synonym. Licit means lawful, laudatory means praising, and lanky means tall and thin.
"Turgid" means swollen, and of language, pompous or inflated. "Concise", "simple" and "plain" are close to its opposite.

words.sentence: Her dog can climb \(\underline{\text{under}}\) the fence.
words.solution: "Under" means below; its opposite is "over" (above). Beneath is a synonym, behind is a different position, and sink is a verb.

words.sentence: Most of the decisions taken by the officer were \(\underline{\text{unjust}}\).
words.solution: 'Unjust' means not based on or behaving according to what is right. Its antonym is correct/fair. Matches option C: correct.

words.sentence: \(\underline{\text{Unrest}}\) in some pockets made the city dwellers confine themselves at home.
words.solution: Answer: D. Unrest = disturbance/turbulence/unease. Antonym is Calm. (Turbulence, unease, apprehension are synonyms.)

words.sentence: Read the sentence carefully and select the ANTONYM of the underlined word from the given options. I heard his suggestion but I am quite \(\underline{\text{unsure}}\) about the risks involved in it.
words.solution: Unsure means not certain, so its antonym is certain. Doubtful is a synonym; interested and thoughtful are unrelated.

words.sentence: I was surprised by his \(\underline{\text{urbane}}\) behaviour. Which one of the following alternatives is nearest in meaning to the underlined word in the above sentence ?
words.solution:
Rule: choose the word nearest in meaning. 'Urbane' means polite, courteous and smooth in manner.
Polite has that meaning.
Rural and town relate to places, and proper does not mean courteous.
So the answer is (B) polite.
No official answer key is on file for this paper. This answer was worked out by PYQ Vault, not published by MPSC.

words.sentence: Sheela appeared to be \(\underline{\text{vexed}}\).
words.solution: 'Vexed' means annoyed or worried; the nearest synonym is 'displeased'. Matches option C: displeased.

words.sentence: The \(\underline{\text{vista}}\) of the villages is beautiful.
words.solution: Answer: A. A vista is a view or expansive scene — a landscape.

words.sentence: The thief had very \(\underline{\text{vital}}\) information to pass on to the police.
words.solution: Answer: B. Antonym of 'vital' (essential) is 'inessential'. Crucial, indispensable and fundamental are synonyms of vital.

words.sentence: The imagery used in the poem is \(\underline{\text{vivid}}\).
words.solution: The key concept is synonym identification. 'Vivid' means producing powerful feelings or clear images; 'lively' is the closest synonym. Matches option A: lively.

words.sentence: Replace the underlined word with its synonym to make the sentence more meaningful. Narcotic drug addiction is in \(\underline{\text{vogue}}\) these days, as it is the most popular form of substance abuse.
words.solution: "In vogue" means in fashion, popular at the time, which matches "the most popular form". "Obscurity" is nearly the opposite, and "demand" and "standard" do not mean vogue.

words.sentence: The explosive used is of my own formulation, and I can \(\underline{\text{vouch}}\) for its efficiency.
words.solution: To vouch for something is to confirm or guarantee it. Certify and witness are close in meaning and maintain (assert) is similar; invalidate (show to be false or void) is the opposite.

words.sentence: My energy \(\underline{\text{waned}}\) to see my college team performing poorly in the match.
words.solution: To wane is to decrease or grow weaker. Declined, dimmed and abated are synonyms; grew is the opposite.

words.sentence: People argue about why Venus is so much \(\underline{\text{warmer}}\) than the Earth.
words.solution: The antonym of 'warmer' (higher temperature) is 'colder' (lower temperature). Matches option B: colder.

words.sentence: In the question four alternatives are given for the underlined word in the sentence. Choose the alternative which best expresses the opposite meaning of the word. “Well, what if it is? You are not afraid of anything, you know,” returned the boy, looking \(\underline{\text{wicked}}\).
words.solution: "Wicked" means evil or morally wrong; its opposite is "righteous", morally right. "Evil" and "improper" are close to its meaning, and "clean" is unrelated.

words.sentence: I have thus far sketched the events of my life, but I have not shown how much I have depended on books not only for pleasure and for the \(\underline{\text{wisdom}}\) they bring to all who read, but also for that knowledge which comes to others through their eyes and their ears.
words.solution: Wisdom is deep understanding and sound judgement; insight (a deep understanding of things) is the closest. Folly is its opposite, and clarity and emotion do not mean understanding.

words.sentence: \(\underline{\text{Wooing}}\) everyone over an issue for support will not serve much purpose.
words.solution: Answer: A. 'Wooing' means seeking to win over or persuade; its opposite is 'discouraging'. Encouraging/pursuing/persuading are close in meaning.

words.sentence: His lectures are often \(\underline{\text{wordy}}\) and pointless.
words.solution: Answer: B. Antonym of 'wordy' (using too many words) is 'concise' (brief). Diffuse, garrulous and voluble are synonyms of wordy.
